prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy disease-relevant proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type degraders

statement.case_for: I keep B014 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The scientific case is a new pharmacological principle: a small molecule brings an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a target, and the cell's own machinery removes it catalytically. That extends drug action to proteins without conventional pockets and rests on design-driven chemistry (E3 ligands, linkers, ternary-complex cooperativity), reproduced by many independent groups over two decades. The chair asked whether the missing approved PROTAC means the field is premature. I think the Crews and Deshaies concept and Handa's identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type drugs are one story, induced proximity to an E3 ligase. The cereblon half already has approved, mechanistically explained drugs, so the claim of clinical relevance does not depend on a PROTAC approval. A citation that names both the concept and the mechanism states the credit exactly and does not claim more than the trio did.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weak point. The three-person cap leaves out Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned PROTACs into a rational design discipline, and also Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim. Ito's exclusion next to Handa is awkward because the cereblon identification was a joint paper. If the committee decides PROTACs and glues are two separate achievements, my single-part citation would be too broad, and I would then prefer a plain PROTAC prize with Ciulli to a stretched citation. No degrader is yet approved, and a committee that requires clinical proof for the PROTAC strand itself could defer the whole field.

responses.point: Chabes holds B014 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs a rational design discipline, and that the cereblon and glue lineage is distinct and would be left out.
responses.response: His argument for Ciulli is the strongest case against my own trio, and I take it seriously. I still prefer Handa, for two reasons. First, the chair's question on maturity is answered by the cereblon strand, where drugs are approved and the mechanism is explained, and a Ciulli trio leaves the prize resting on the part of the field that has no approved drug. Second, structure-guided design refined and generalised the concept, while the discovery that thalidomide acts through cereblon was a mechanistic discovery that nobody else could supply. If the committee decides that the PROTAC and glue lineages must be separated, I would vote for his trio over mine, so we differ on how to resolve the main open question and not on the science.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B046 for its mechanistic clarity, three decades of confirmation and clean two-person credit, and answers the chair's question on the 2010 prize by saying the ligand-controlled mechanism makes C-N coupling a conceptual advance and not only a new nucleophile.
responses.response: I accept that the ligand logic (bulky electron-rich phosphines controlling oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination) is a real mechanistic contribution, and that Buchwald and Hartwig deserve the clean credit he describes. Where I differ is that the catalytic cycle and the logic of ligand control were already in the cross-coupling prize, and the step here is to a new bond class inside the same framework. Targeted degradation changes what a drug does, not only how a molecule is built. I would not object to B046 as a prize, and I keep it as my first alternative because its credit is better settled than ours. On the evidence question the chair put, I would move to B046 only if the committee concludes that B014 cannot be allocated defensibly within three names.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B046 and concedes in his own file that the 2010 prize overlap is the main reservation, that B014 had stronger novelty claims, and that B014 might be preferred if its PROTAC and glue strands can be allocated cleanly in three names.
responses.response: His own condition is the one I try to meet: PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and cereblon mechanism (Handa) form a three-name allocation with a stated rationale for each, even though it excludes Ciulli and Ito. I think that is clean enough to meet his test, because each laureate is tied to a distinct, documented step in one principle. I also share his worry about Kosugi, Migita, Guram and Rennels under B046, which is a precursor-credit problem of the same kind as ours and shows that neither configuration avoids exclusions. I do not think credit clarity alone should decide between novelty and tidiness, and I would ask him whether the novelty point he conceded would move him if the citation is written as above.

responses.point: The chair prefers Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (B027) for its unambiguous two-author credit and four decades of use, while admitting that it is physics-flavoured, that computational chemistry was recognised in 2013 and 2024, and that its day-to-day chemical impact is less visible.
responses.response: The two-author credit is a real advantage, and I do not doubt the method's maturity. My reservation is about the weight of the achievement for the chemistry community. Most of its use is in condensed-phase and materials modelling, and as he says, the committee has just recognised computation twice. I would put a new drug modality with approved mechanistic relatives ahead of a third computational prize. I also appreciate that he lists B014 as his alternative and flags the three-person cut across lineages as an open problem. I hope my attribution rationale, which ties each name to a separate documented step, gives him a basis for supporting it if B027 does not gain support.

responses.point: Sparr prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B060), citing lipid self-assembly physical chemistry, pKa-controlled charge and endosomal escape, and clinical validation through siRNA and mRNA products, but she acknowledges credit spread over at least six people, patent-driven priority disputes and overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.
responses.response: I find the physical chemistry persuasive, and I keep B060 as my second alternative because its clinical validation is solid. My concern is the same as hers: with Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan outside the Cullis, Hope and Madden trio, and patents shaping the priority record, I cannot see a three-name allocation that the scientific literature alone would support, and the 2023 prize already honoured the nucleic-acid payload side. B014 has a more tractable allocation problem, even though it is imperfect.

uncertainties: Whether the PROTAC concept and cereblon-mediated molecular glues are one achievement (induced proximity to an E3 ligase) or two that should not be merged.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name, and whether the exclusion of Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim can be defended in the citation.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC makes the field premature for a majority of the committee.
Whether B046 is a conceptually new advance over the 2010 prize, which would justify it as the better-credited alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to disclose. None of the shortlisted candidates is a current or former mentor, colleague or collaborator of mine, and my postdoctoral mentors are not on the shortlist. My work on designed peptides and nanoparticle biosensors is only loosely related to B014 and does not give me a stake in any configuration. I note that my own preference has not changed since round 1, and I hold it for scientific reasons and not because of the count of supporters.
